findings.title: Polymarket status: exchange in cancel-only mode while investigating incident
findings.summary_md: Polymarket's status page posted an incident at 18:05 UTC on October 29, 2026, reporting the predictions trading API in major outage and the exchange in cancel-only mode with relayer actions paused. Subsequent updates stated the issue affecting Polymarket.com was identified and fixed, that a third-party provider was compromised and referred to law enforcement, that affected users would be made whole, and that trading resumed around 19:05 UTC.

findings.title: world on X: Polymarket frontend may be hacked
findings.summary_md: An X post reported that Polymarket's frontend may have been compromised, with trading restricted to cancel-only mode and relayer actions paused. It cited user reports of wallets being drained and a possible frontend compromise before Polymarket's public confirmation.

findings.title: StarPlatinum on X: Polymarket users drained
findings.summary_md: An X post claimed Polymarket users were being drained in real time, with roughly $2.68 million reportedly stolen within an hour. It described hundreds of withdrawals routed through Polymarket's own deposit wallet infrastructure.

findings.title: Wu Blockchain on X: multiple Polymarket users report stolen funds
findings.summary_md: Wu Blockchain reported that multiple Polymarket users described unauthorized fund transfers, with some claiming losses of hundreds of thousands of dollars. Users suspected a possible frontend compromise while the cause remained unconfirmed, and Polymarket had entered cancel-only mode and paused relayer actions.

findings.title: Polymarket Traders on X: third-party provider compromised
findings.summary_md: Polymarket's official trading account confirmed it identified and fixed an issue affecting Polymarket.com, stating that one of its third-party providers was compromised and the matter was referred to law enforcement. It said affected users would be made whole and trading was temporarily halted out of an abundance of caution.

findings.title: Polymarket Breach Alert: Wallet-Draining Code Found in a Third-Party Script
findings.summary_md: Hudson Rock reported finding wallet-draining JavaScript in a DebugBear real-user-monitoring script associated with Polymarket, published 18:33 UTC on October 29, 2026. The code reads account context, locates the trading client and signer, inspects the portfolio, and attempts to sell or transfer assets, while Polymarket's production build records removal of the DebugBear RUM integration.
